verses.1: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still confined in the courtyard of the guard, saying:
verses.2: "This is what the LORD, the maker, the former, the one who establishes, says: I am the LORD, and my name is his."
verses.3: "Call to me and I will answer you and will reveal to you great and mighty things that you have not known."
verses.4: "For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning the houses of this city and the houses of the kings of Judah that have been set on siegeworks and on the sword:
verses.5: coming to fight against the Chaldeans, and filling it with the corpses of the men I have struck in my anger and in my wrath, and from whose face I have turned away because of all their evil.
verses.6: "Behold, I will raise up a healer and will bring relief to it, and I will reveal and heal it, and I will give them abundance of peace and faith.
verses.7: "And I will restore the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Israel, and I will build them as in the beginning.
verses.8: "And I will cleanse them from all their iniquities with which they have sinned against me, and I will forgive all their sins with which they have sinned against me and turned away from me.
verses.9: "And it will become for me a name of joy, a song of praise, and a glory to all the nations of the earth who will hear all the good that I do for them, and they will fear and tremble at all the good and at all the peace that I do for it."
verses.10: "This is what the LORD says: Again there will be heard in this place, which you say is desolate, without people and without animals, in the cities of Judah and in the outskirts of Jerusalem that lie waste because there is no person and no dweller and no animal:
verses.11: the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the sound of a bridegroom and the sound of a bride, the sound of those who say, 'Give thanks to the LORD of Hosts, for the LORD is good! His steadfast love endures forever!' They will bring thanksgiving into the house of the LORD, for I will restore the captivity of the land as in the beginning," says the LORD.
verses.12: "This is what the LORD of Hosts says: Again there will be shepherds' encampments in this desolate place, where there is no person, and in all its cities sheep will lie down.
verses.13: "In the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the lowland, and in the cities of the Negev, in the land of Benjamin, and around Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, again the sheep will pass before the one who counts," says the LORD.
verses.14: "Behold, days are coming," says the LORD, "and I will fulfill the good word I spoke to the house of Israel and to the house of Judah.
verses.15: "In those days and at that time I will raise up for David a sprout of righteousness, and he will do justice and righteousness on the earth.
verses.16: "In those days Judah will be saved and Jerusalem will dwell securely, and this is what it will be called: The LORD our Righteousness."
verses.17: "For this is what the LORD says: David will not lack an heir on the throne of the house of Israel.
verses.18: "And to the Levitical priests, my ministers, there will never be lacking an offerer of burnt offering and one who brings a grain offering and performs a sacrifice every day."
verses.19: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying:
verses.20: "This is what the LORD says: If my covenant for day and night fails, and if day and night do not come at their appointed times,
verses.21: then my covenant with David my servant will also be broken so that he has no son reigning on his throne, and my covenant with the Levitical priests, my ministers.
verses.22: "As the host of the heavens cannot be numbered and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the offspring of David my servant and the Levitical priests, my ministers.
verses.23: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying:
verses.24: "Have you not seen what this people has said, saying, 'The two families that the LORD chose, he has rejected them, and our people are despised, no longer a nation before them'?"
verses.25: "This is what the LORD says: If my covenant with day and night is not established, and if I have not set the laws of heaven and earth—
verses.26: then also I will reject the offspring of Jacob and David my servant from my descendants, from the offspring of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For I will restore their captivity and will have mercy on them."

notes:
Notes  
- v. 2: "my name is his" – Hebrew is ambiguous, possibly "my name is his" or "his name is mine," but the context suggests the emphasis is on the LORD's own naming as creator.  
- v. 16: "The LORD our Righteousness" – The Hebrew uses "tsidqenu," which is translated as a proper noun here.  
- v. 25–26: The structure of the conditional is complex; the translation follows the logical flow that God's covenant with Israel remains intact, paralleling the unchanging nature of day and night.
